"The dead area," Crain told them, "is a region of space ninety thousand miles across within Neptune's orbit, in which the ordinary gravitational attractions of the solar system are dead. This is because in that region the pulls of the sun and the outer planets exactly balance each other. Because of that, anything in the dead-area, will stay in there until time ends, unless it has power of its own.

arxiv-1806-02098.title: k-medoids and p-median clustering are solvable in polynomial time for a 2d Pareto front Journal: Preprint
arxiv-1806-02098.creator: Nicolas Dupin, Frank Nielsen, El-Ghazali Talbi
arxiv-1806-02098.description: Abstract This paper examines a common extension of k-medoids and k-median clustering in the case of a two-dimensional Pareto front, as generated by bi-objective optimization approaches. A characterization of optimal clusters is provided, which allows to solve the optimization problems to optimality in polynomial time using a common dynamic programming algorithm.

arxiv-1906-05173.title: Multi-local Collaborative AutoEncoder Journal: Journal of Knowledge-Based Systems
arxiv-1906-05173.creator: Jielei Chu, Hongjun Wang, Jing Liu, Zhiguo Gong, Tianrui Li
arxiv-1906-05173.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Jielei Chu, Hongjun Wang, Jing Liu, Zhiguo Gong, Tianrui Li. The excellent performance of representation learning of autoencoders have attracted considerable interest in various applications. However, the structure and multi-local collaborative relationships of unlabeled data are ignored in their encoding procedure that limits the capability of feature extraction. This paper presents a Multi-local Collaborative AutoEncoder (MC-AE), which consists of novel multi-local collaborative representation RBM (mcrRBM) and multi-local collaborative representation GRBM (mcrGRBM) models.

arxiv-2109-00936.title: Impact of Attention on Adversarial Robustness of Image Classification Models
arxiv-2109-00936.creator: Prachi Agrawal, Sanjay Kumar Sonbhadra, Narinder Singh Punn, Sonali Agarwal
arxiv-2109-00936.description: Abstract Adversarial attacks against deep learning models have gained significant attention and recent works have proposed explanations for the existence of adversarial examples and techniques to defend the models against these attacks. Attention in computer vision has been used to incorporate focused learning of important features and has led to improved accuracy.

arxiv-2112-09687.title: Light Field Neural Rendering
arxiv-2112-09687.creator: Mohammed Suhail 1,2 Carlos Esteves 4 Leonid Sigal 1,2,3 Ameesh Makadia 4 suhail33@cs.ubc.ca machc@google.com lsigal@cs.ubc.ca makadia@google.com 1 University of British Columbia 2 Vector Institute for AI 3 Canada CIFAR AI Chair 4 Google
arxiv-2112-09687.description: Abstract Classical light field rendering for novel view synthesis can accurately reproduce view-dependent effects such as reflection, refraction, and translucency, but requires a dense view sampling of the scene. Methods based on geometric reconstruction need only sparse views, but cannot accurately model non-Lambertian effects. We introduce a model that combines the strengths and mitigates the limitations of these two directions.

arxiv-2304-03695.title: Principal Component Analysis of Ground Level Enhancement of Cosmic Ray Events
arxiv-2304-03695.creator: R.E. Ugwoke, A. A. Ubachukwu, J. O. Urama, O. Okike, J. A. Alhassan, A. E. Chukwude
arxiv-2304-03695.description: Abstract We applied principal component analysis (PCA) to the study of five ground level enhancement (GLE) of cosmic ray (CR) events. The nature of the multivariate data involved makes PCA a useful tool for this study. A subroutine program written and implemented in R software environment generated interesting principal components.

It allows to describe the relations between division points, isogenies, and discriminants both for a fixed Drinfeld module of rank r r for the above data, or for the corresponding modular forms.

arxiv-2402-08156.title: Differentially Private Distributed Inference
arxiv-2402-08156.creator: Marios Papachristou, M. Amin Rahimian
arxiv-2402-08156.description: Abstract How can agents exchange information to learn from each other despite their privacy needs and security concerns? Consider healthcare centers that want to collaborate on a multicenter clinical trial, but are concerned about sharing sensitive patient information. Preserving individual privacy and enabling efficient social learning are both important desiderata, but they seem fundamentally at odds.

arxiv-2405-19197.description: Abstract . The A-polynomial of a knot is defined in terms of SL ⁡ ( 2 , ℂ ) \mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{C}) representations of the knot group, and encodes information about essential surfaces in the knot complement. In 2005, Dunfield–Garoufalidis and Boyer–Zhang proved that it detects the unknot using Kronheimer–Mrowka’s work on the Property P conjecture.

arxiv-2602-05845.title: Self-Supervised Learning with a Multi-Task Latent Space Objective
arxiv-2602-05845.creator: Pierre-François De Plaen, Abhishek Jha, Luc Van Gool, Tinne Tuytelaars, Marc Proesmans
arxiv-2602-05845.description: Abstract Self-supervised learning (SSL) methods based on Siamese networks learn visual representations by aligning different views of the same image. The multi-crop strategy, which incorporates small local crops to global ones, enhances many SSL frameworks but causes instability in predictor-based architectures such as BYOL, SimSiam, and MoCo v3.

arxiv-2602-16315.title: The Diversity Paradox revisited: Systemic Effects of Feedback Loops in Recommender Systems
arxiv-2602-16315.creator: Gabriele Barlacchi, Margherita Lalli, Emanuele Ferragina, Fosca Giannotti, Dino Pedreschi, Luca Pappalardo
arxiv-2602-16315.description: Abstract Recommender systems shape individual choices through feedback loops in which user behavior and algorithmic recommendations coevolve over time. The systemic effects of these loops remain poorly understood, in part due to unrealistic assumptions in existing simulation studies. We propose a feedback-loop model that captures implicit feedback, periodic retraining, probabilistic adoption of recommendations, and heterogeneous recommender systems.

pmc-11420593.title: Treatment patterns in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus in New Zealand
pmc-11420593.creator: Chunhuan Lao, Philippa Van Dantzig, Nikki Tugnet, Ross Lawrenson, Douglas White
pmc-11420593.description: ObjectivesThis study aims to explore the treatment pattern of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) in Aotearoa/New Zealand.MethodsSLE patients were linked to the pharmaceutical dispensing data. The use of publicly funded anti-malarials, immunomodulators, biologics, glucocorticoids and bisphosphonates were compared by gender, ethnicity, age group, socioeconomic status and year of SLE identification.

pmc-11644526.title: Online Monitoring of Catalytic Processes by Fiber-Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy
pmc-11644526.creator: John T Kelly, Christopher J Koch, Robert Lascola, Tyler Guin, Michael P Buric, Nageswara R Lalam
pmc-11644526.description: An innovative solution for real-time monitoring of reactions within confined spaces, optimized for Raman spectroscopy applications, is presented. This approach involves the utilization of a hollow-core waveguide configured as a compact flow cell, serving both as a conduit for Raman excitation and scattering and seamlessly integrating into the effluent stream of a cracking catalytic reactor.

pmc-12503789.title: Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis Successfully Treated with Combination of Thalidomide and Corticosteroid
pmc-12503789.creator: Nadia Ayu Mulansari, Abdul Muthalib, Cynthia Kurniawan
pmc-12503789.description: Langerhans cell histiocytosis (LCH) is rare disease characterised by clonal proliferation of Langerhans cells. The effectiveness of the current standard of treatment for LCH has not been proved in prospective trials, and 50% of patients treated with the current standard of treatment were unresponsive.

pmc-12665021.title: Challenges in diagnosing common tumors at uncommon sites
pmc-12665021.creator: Rajyalakshmi Rallapalli, Kusa Raju Pyla, Beulah Priscilla Maddirala, Kishore Kumar Ch, Ganesh Basina
pmc-12665021.description: Rare tumors are a heterogeneous group of neoplasms with low incidence and are usually difficult to diagnose. Certain tumors that are common at specific anatomical locations rarely occur at unexpected locations and cause diagnostic challenges. Although histopathology is central to the diagnosis of these lesions, as with any tumor, ancillary techniques such as immunohistochemistry and molecular studies are often essential.

pmc-13157789.title: Congo’s conflicts, minerals and microbes: planetary health implications
pmc-13157789.creator: Shahul H Ebrahim, John Ditekemena, Barrak Alahmad, Ann-Christine Duhaime, Dieudonné Mwamba, Ziad A Memish
pmc-13157789.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The abrupt re-escalation of the three-decade conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) in January 2025, the July peace deal and new mineral extraction agreements highlight the Congo Basin’s global significance. Known as the world’s largest rare mineral reserve, the ‘second lung of the planet’, and a hotspot for emerging infectious diseases, the region embodies critical planetary health challenges.

On ultrasound examination, an increase in uterine volume and a mass measuring 3.

pmc-13235959.title: Adenoma receptors and histologic characteristics determining management outcomes
pmc-13235959.creator: Luiz Eduardo Wildemberg, Mônica R Gadelha
pmc-13235959.description: Patient responses to medical therapy for acromegaly are variable. Adenoma features, including histologic characteristics and receptor density, are closely associated with distinct clinical behavior and therapeutic outcomes. Densely granulated pure somatotropinomas respond more favorably to somatostatin receptor subtype 2 (SST2)-selective ligands (octreotide and lanreotide) compared with sparsely granulated adenomas.

pmc-13599215.title: Limb-bud and heart (LBH) promotes expansion and survival of esophageal adenocarcinoma cells
pmc-13599215.creator: Sydnee Fo, Heng Lu, Lei Chen, Dunfa Peng, Zheng Chen, Wael El-Rifai, Farah Ballout
pmc-13599215.description: BackgroundEsophageal Adenocarcinoma (EAC) is an aggressive malignancy with poor prognosis. The rising incidence of EAC in the past few decades underscores the need to better understand the molecular features of EAC. The role of the transcriptional co-factor Limb-Bud and Heart (LBH), implicated in embryonic development and Wnt signaling, remains unclearly characterized in gastrointestinal cancers.

pmc-13645431.title: Conditional pathways to loneliness in older adults with vision impairment: a decision-tree analysis
pmc-13645431.creator: Ya-Han Chang, Silvia Sörensen, Michelle Putnam
pmc-13645431.description: Background and ObjectivesThe prevalence of vision impairment continues to increase globally due to population growth and aging. Among older adults with vision impairment, loneliness is common. Prior studies assessing loneliness risk have relied on regression-based approaches, which may not capture complex, heterogeneous conditional pathways.
